summary: Geo-tagged rate anchoring caused unexpected tariff removal and invoice delta
description: Issue summary: Customer reported an unexpected removal of a sustainability discount tied to geo-tag routing which resulted in a ~12% higher invoice line for two daily billing windows. Impact: NimbleRetail observed a sudden invoice delta of $4,800 on the March 3 billing run and flagged missing provisional credits. Environment: Dedicated deployment (APAC primary, EU fallback) using geo-tag routing + per-region pricing overrides. Expected: geo-tagged requests should preserve applied 'sustainability' rate tag and receive discounted tariff. Observed: for a subset of requests routed through the SIN edge between 03:10-04:45 UTC the sustainability tag was absent in postbacks, causing default tariff to apply and final invoice to reflect the higher rate. Customer asked for explanation and provisional credit while we investigate.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sends model requests via dedicated pool with geo-tag header set to apac-sin
2) Our routing sends traffic to SIN edge which should append rate_tag=eco-green before postback
3) Postback shows rate_tag empty for affected requests during the 03:10-04:45 UTC window
4) Billing pipeline applied default tariff to those postbacks and invoice generated with higher line item
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support: reproduced missing rate_tag in postback subset; not all SIN requests affected
SRE checked edge proxy config rotations between 02:50-03:20 UTC; there was a config push to rate-tag normalizer service (INT-412)
Billing-engine team looked at postback enrichment: enrichment worker retried and dropped tag when enrichment table returned 404 for a short window
Hypothesis: normalization rollout failed to map new geo-ids to eco-green tag, causing enrichment to return null and downstream billing to fall back to default tariff
Estimate of impact: ~38k tokens affected across two models; gross delta approximately $4,800; potential rounding variance at invoice generation
Cross-reference: console-estimate for affected route shows discount applied when tag present; mismatch only for affected postbacks
comments: 2026-03-10 10:04 - Aisha (Support): Opening ticket after NimbleRetail escalated via account manager. Attached CSV of sample request_ids and invoice lines.
2026-03-10 12:21 - Tomas (SRE): Noted a rate-normalizer deployment at 02:59 UTC. Pulling deploy logs and rate-cache snapshots; assigning INT-412 to track rollout fix.
2026-03-10 14:02 - Billing Eng (Marcel): Found enrichment-worker logs showing 404 against geo-map-v2 for 03:05-03:18 UTC. Worker treats missing mapping as null tag.
2026-03-11 09:40 - Aisha (Support): Customer accepted provisional credit while engineering confirms root cause. Requested ETA for ledger correction and customer-facing explanation.

2026-03-12 08:15 - Tomas (SRE): Root cause confirmed: rate-tag normalizer schema change omitted legacy geo key 'SIN-1' during rollout. Rollback performed at 03:22 UTC. Billing team preparing ledger adjustments and provisional credit.

2026-03-12 10:01 - Support (Aisha): Notified customer of provisional credit of $4,800 applied to account pending final invoice reconciliation. Customer requested confirmation once final ledger correction posts.
resolution: Workaround/fix: Rolled back rate-tag normalizer rollout (INT-412) at 03:22 UTC which restored mapping for SIN-1. Billing workaround: provisional credit of $4,800 applied to NimbleRetail account on 2026-03-12 pending final reprocessing. Permanent fix: rate-tag normalizer now includes integration test for legacy geo keys and enrichment worker updated to log and preserve previous tag on 404 instead of nulling. Follow-ups: billing will reprocess affected postbacks and publish corrected invoice lines; runbook updated at confluence.redwood/KB/geo-tagged-rate-anchoring-runbook; PR created github.com/redwood-inference/billing-engine/pull/742 for ledger replay orchestration. Customer follow-up scheduled for 2026-03-13.
